title: Rabbi Chiyya bar Lulayni (Lulayva, Lulayta)
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In Taanit 25a it is told that Rabbi Chiya bar Lulayni heard those clouds saying, "Let us go and pour water in Ammon and Moab." He said before Him, "Master of the Universe, when You gave the Torah to Your people Israel, You went around to all the nations of the world and they did not accept it, and now You give them rain? Throw it here!" They poured it where he was. And there he expounded: "If 'palm' was stated, why was 'cedar' stated?" etc. In the Yerushalmi, Avodah Zarah beginning of ch. 2, he said in the name of Rabbi Hoshaya; and in Ketubot ch. 13 halakhah 2 and Nedarim ch. 4 halakhah 2, Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Bun and Rabbi Chiya bar Lulayno both say in the name of Shmuel; and in Nazir ch. 4, end of halakhah 4, they both say in the name of (Rabbi) Shmi; and in Orlah beginning of ch. 2, Rabbi Chiya bar Lulayva said to Rabbi Chananya.

We also find that he had students, as in Challah end of ch. 2, Yoma ch. 2 beginning of halakhah 2, Nedarim beginning of ch. 3, Nazir ch. 5 halakhah 3, Shevuot ch. 8 halakhah 3: "the students of Rabbi Chiya bar Lulayta," etc.

notes.text: Lulayni, Lulayno, Lulayva and Lulayta are retained as the notice’s variant forms.

The consulted Taanit 25a gives the clouds, Ammon and Moab, the demand to pour here, and the palm/cedar homily, which continues at the beginning of 25b. Lulayni and the other supplied forms remain occurrence-specific readings; the separate Jerusalem Talmud transmissions are not converted into one canonical name.
